The source-text matching and exact verify-line checks resolve the earlier reversal, conditional and fabricated-quote objections. However, index >= last_matched_index permits an instruction to be repeated indefinitely. An in-memory reproduction accepted 'Transfer 100 dollars. Then transfer 100 dollars.' against the single claim 'Transfer 100 dollars.': matched indices=[0, 0], unsupported remainder=''. This authorizes an additional transaction in both generation and post-polish validation. None of the listed tests checks repeated consumption of one claim.

verdicts.evidence: The rebuttal correctly establishes existing spelling normalization, and canonicalizing before narrative generation prevents the earlier verify-line rewrite. But applying canonicalize_terms to serialized JSON corrupts structural keys. Using the actual implementation with title 'Inspect the Segements collection' and transcript {"segments":[{"text":"Inspect the Segments collection.","start":0}]} changed the key to 'segements'; _parse_json_segments then raised ValueError: malformed JSON transcript: 'segments'. consistency.py:293 replaces words throughout every field, while transcript.py:144 requires the original key. The proposed placement catch followed by _claims_for_narrative([], narration) would then treat JSON syntax as prose claims, contrary to F-04. The listed tests do not exercise photo JSON canonicalization.
verdicts.command: Read-only python -B - probe calling canonicalize_terms and _parse_json_segments produced {"segements": [{"text": "Inspect the Segements collection.", "start": 0}]} and ValueError malformed JSON transcript: 'segments'.
verdicts.amendment: Parse JSON before canonicalization and transform only segment text values, preserving keys, timestamps and structure; perform placement from those parsed segments or safely reserialized data. Never send serialized JSON to the plain-text claim helper or _narration_to_claims fallback. On placement failure, derive fallback claims from parsed segment texts. Add this exact photo-build regression asserting successful placement, configured narrative-model calls, and no JSON syntax in claims or exports.
